text: Maratha State and Confederacy *Shivaji was born at the fort of Shivner in 1627 or 1630 AD. He adopted the title of Chhatrapati after his coronation in 1674 AD. He made Raigarh his capital. *Pandit Vishweshwar alias ‘Gangabhatta’, a great scholar of that era, declared Shivaji a Kshatriya on his coronation. Shivaji died in 1680 AD at the age of 53 or 50 years. *The reason for the rise of Maratha power was its residents. *The unity of the people on the ground of caste, language, religion, literature and residence ﬂ ourished the feeling of nationalism among them. The geographical conditions of Maharashtra were helpful in ﬂ ourishing the Maratha power. *The high leadership quality of Shivaji and other Maratha leaders contributed to the rise of Maratha power. *In 1659 AD, the Sultan of Bijapur sent his experienced and trusted commander Afzal Khan for suppression of Shivaji, but the diplomat and clever Shivaji killed him. Indian History General Studies B–317 *Treaty of Purandar was signed between Shivaji and Jai Singh in 1665 AD. Shivaji was imprisioned in Jaipur Bhawan at Agra when he escaped from the custody of Mughals. Aurangzeb imprisoned Shivaji in 1666 AD at Agra. *‘Ashtapradhan’ was the Council of eight Ministers constituted by Shivaji for Maratha administration. The eight ministers were – (i) Peshwa - Prime Minister of the King . (ii) Amatya - Finance and Revenue Minister . (iii) Waqianavis/Mantri - Interior Minister, managing internal aﬀ airs, especially intelligence and espionage . (iv) Sachiv/Surunavis - Responsible for all correspondence. (v) Sumant/Dabir - Foreign Minister . (vi) Senapati/Sar-i-Naubat - Maintenance of appointments, organization and food supply of military. (vii) Pandit Rao - Appointed for religious aid. (viii) Nyayadhish - Chief Justice. *Rajaram led the Marathas as a representative of Shahu from 1689 AD to 1700 AD. After the death of Rajaram, his widow Tarabai continued the struggle with the Mughals placing his four year old son Shivaji-II on the throne. At the time of Aurangzeb’s death, the Maratha leadership was in the hands of Tarabai. *After Sambhaji, the power of Maratha kingdom came in the hands of Balaji Vishwanath who made the administration easy and convenient. *Maratha Chhatrapati Shahu appointed Balaji to the post of Peshwa. November 1773 was an important day not only for Balaji but also for the whole Marathas as the power was transferred from Chhatrapati to the Peshwa. *Balaji Vishwanath reigned from 1713 AD to 1720 AD. *Shahu appointed the elder son of Balaji Vishwanath, Bajirao - I as Peshwa whose tenure was from 1720 AD to 1740 AD. *Balaji Bajirao ruled from 1740 AD to 1761 AD after the death of Bajirao. Madhavrao’s tenure was from 1761 AD to 1772 AD. *After the death of Madhavrao in 1772 AD, his brother Narayanrao became a victim of the conspiracy of his uncle Raghunathrao, who himself wanted to became Peshwa. *By the time of Balaji Bajirao, the Post of Peshwa became hereditary. Previously the power was in the hands of the Chhatrapati, but now the centre of power shifted in the hands of Peshwas. By the treaty of Sangola in 1750 AD, the Maratha King became a “do nothing king” and just the Mayor of a palace and Peshwa emerged as the real and eﬀ ective head of Maratha confederacy. *Saranzami syatem was related to land revenue in Maratha period. The land given under Saranzami system was provided for the livelihood of Maratha Jagirdar during the Maratha period. *In January, 1757 AD, Ahemad Shah Abdali entered Delhi and looted up to Agra and Mathura. Before returning to his motherland, he appointed Alamgir II as Emperor, Imadulmulk as prime minister and Rohilla leader Najib-Ud-Daulah as his chief agent and Mir Bakshi of the Empire. *The third battle of Panipat was fought between Maratha Sadashivrao Bhau and Afghan invader Ahmad Shah Abdali on 14th January 1761. Marathas were badly defeated by Afghans in this battle. According to Kashiraj Pandit, a historian who was eyewitness of this battle “two pearls have been dissolved, 22 gold coins have been lost and of the silver and copper the total cannot be cast up” that was the message which was sent to Balaji Bajirao in encrypted form by a merchant after this agonising defeat of Marathas. The immediate reason for the battle of Panipat was the Ahmed Shah Abdali’s desire to avenge Marathas as they expelled his Viceroy Timur Shah from Lahore. *Ahilyabai was a Maratha ruler from Holkar dynasty. Holkars belong to Indore. 1. Which is/are correct reasons of Maratha’s Rise? (a) Religious Consciousness (b) Geographical Security (c) Political awakening (d) High quality of leadership (e) all of the above U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1992 Ans. (e) All factors are correct for the rise of Marathas. Maratha’s rise was neither speciﬁ c nor the result of unstable circumstances generated in a speciﬁ c period. The reason for Maratha rise was its residents, whose nationalism was on the ground of unity, caste, language, religion, literature and habitat. The geographical conditions of Maharashtra were helpful in ﬂ ourishing the Maratha power. The high leadership quality of Shivaji and other Maratha leaders contributed to the rise of Maratha power. 2. Disintegration of the Mughal Empire *After the death of Aurangzeb in 1707 AD his 63-year-old son Muazzam (Shah Alam) ascended the throne adopting the name of ‘Bahadur Shah’. He ruled in the period between 1707-1712 AD. *He was given the title of ‘Shahe Bekhabar’ by Khaﬁ Khan. *Jahandar Shah was the ﬁ rst emperor in the Mughal dynasty, who proved to be highly disqualiﬁ ed for governance. He ascended the throne with the help of Zulﬁ qar Khan. He was defeated and killed by his nephew Farrukh Siyar in a battle in 1713 AD. *Farrukh Siyar issued a decree in which he granted duty - free trading facilities to the British in Bengal in 1717. It was mentioned in the contract that the East India Company could trade without duty (charge) after paying the annual tax of 3000. *Muhammad Shah (1719 - 1748 ) was the last Mughal emperor to sit on Peacock throne (built by Shah Jahan). During his reign, Nadir Shah attacked India in 1739 AD and defeated Mughals in the battle of Karnal. The contemporary historian Anand Ram Mukhlis wrote, "Nadir Shah took sixty thousand rupees, many thousands of gold coins, gold of one crore rupee, jewels of ﬁ fty crore, Kohinoor and peacock throne with him to Iran." *Muhammad Shah (1719-1748) spends most of his time in watching animal ﬁ ght. People called him Rangeela due to his obsession towards wine and beauty and apathy towards administration. A group of eunuchs and ladies dominated in Mughal Darbar during the regime of Muhammad Shah. *The tenure of Shah Alam-II was from 1759 to 1806. His real name was Ali Gauhar. English captured Delhi in 1803 during his tenure. *The last Mughal emperor was Bahadur Shah Zafar / Bahadur Shah II (1837 -1857 AD). His father’s name was Akbar -II (1806 -1837 AD). He was called as the "Emperor without Empire". *Ibrahim Jauq and Asad Ullah Khan Ghalib taught poetry to Bahadur Shah Zafar. Hasan Askari was his spiritual teacher. *Bahadur Shah Zafar got Rs 1 lakh per month from the East India Company as pension, Rs 15 lakh for his other estates and one thousand rupees for regular family expenses. He died in 1862 AD . *Chin Qilich Khan aka Nizam-ul-Mulk founded the independent Kingdom of Hyderabad in 1724. Nizam became the real king after the death of the Mughal governor Mubarij Khan in the battle of Shakur - Khera of Deccan, 1724. *Sawai Jai Singh (1681 - 1743 A.D.) of Amber was a Rajput king of the 18th century. *He established ‘Jaipur’ city and made it the centre of science and art. *He built well-equipped observatories in Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura and Varanasi. He translated ‘‘Euclid's Geometry” in Sanskrit. *He organized two Ashvamedh sacriﬁ ces during his reign. 1. Who succeeded Aurangzeb after his death in 1707 A.D.? (a) Bahadur Shah- I (b) Jahandar Shah (c) Muhammad Shah (d) Akbar- II U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2012 Ans. (a) After the death of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb, his sixty-three years old son Muazzam (Shah Alam) ascended the throne adopting the name of Bahadur Shah in 1707. He ruled over the duration of 1707-1712. 2. How did the Mughal Emperor Jahandar Shah’s reign come to an early end ?
